content.text:
The Bracket Bust campaign ran from March 30 through the end of April 5 Central time, and it came in under budget. Both ad groups were scheduled to end at midnight Central on April 5, and I confirmed they're past their end time.

**Recap**

| | Spend | Impressions | Link clicks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Post A (the straight giveaway post, 2169303362567964049) | $148.33 | 206,198 | 54 |
| Post B (the "bracket busted" post, 2169484556499105334) | $321.86 | 244,365 | 188 |
| **Total** | **$470.19** | **450,563** | **242** |

The total is $79.81 under your $550 budget. The overall cost was about $1.94 per link click.

**What I did**
- **Setup:** I made one campaign with two ad groups, one per approved post. Both targeted the US only, ages 21 and over, which meets X's alcohol policy. I didn't write any new posts.
- **Optimization:** Post B got clicks at about a third of A's cost per click: about $1.71 versus $2.75 over the week. By April 3, B had 74 clicks against A's 44 and a lower cost per click. I moved budget toward it in two steps, April 1 and April 3, so B ended with 78% of clicks.
- **Underspend:** B's April 3 cap of $55 a day, with delivery spread evenly through the day, didn't use the full budget. That's why $79.81 is left over.

**Caveats for matching against your entry count**
- X had no pixel on your site, so I optimized for link clicks, not entries. Clicks are the closest proxy I could measure. B's lead in clicks may not carry over to entries, so check your own data on that.
- Link clicks on X usually run higher than landing-page sessions, because some people bounce before the page loads. Expect your site analytics to show somewhat fewer visits than the 242 clicks.
- The "engagements" numbers in X's reports (3,140 in total) include likes, expands and other interactions. Only link clicks are comparable to entries.

I'm happy to compare your final entry count against these figures if you send it over.
